in_text_mentions: psychomotor development, generalized hypotonia, low height, and hypertrichosis. Her weight was 8,7 kg (-2,2 SD) and her height was 72 cm (-3,83 SD). Physical examination revealed round facies, thick eyebrows, synophrys, long eyelashes, downslanted palpebral fissures, hypertelorism, long philtrum, Dennis Morgan folds, and excessive thick facial hair mainly in the frontal region (Fig. 1). Generalized hypertrichosis was present and more pronounced on the back and around the mammillae (Fig. 2). Other findings included mild generalized hypotonia, broad feet, and irritability without hyperactivity.

A: Panel A shows congenital eyelid anomalies including small palpebral fissures and ptosis in a 1-year-old patient, consistent with WSS. B: Panel B shows thick eyebrows, hair, and a long philtrum on a patient presenting with WSS features at age 7. C: Panel C displays hypertrichosis (excess body hair) on the back, a known WSS feature. D: Panel D shows craniofacial features including a narrow high palate and low hairline, associated with WSS. E: Panel E shows external ear deformity and low-set ears, a key feature of WSS. F: Panel F shows hypertrichosis on the back of the patient, consistent with WSS.
